ops.title: service/keepalive.go notLoaded() never fires in production — interface assertion cannot match worker.ExitError
ops.description:
Found by the Phase-0 invariant census (empirically, with a probe built against the real package), **verified independently at `origin/main` = `1d55b2a`** before filing.

## The defect

`service/keepalive.go:529-535`:

```go
func notLoaded(err error) bool {
	var exit interface{ ExitCode() int }
	if !errors.As(err, &exit) {
		return false
	}
	return exit.ExitCode() == launchctlNotLoadedExit || exit.ExitCode() == launchctlNotFoundExit
}
```

It asserts `interface{ ExitCode() int }` — a **method**. But the error it actually receives is `*worker.ExitError`, and `worker/pool.go:80,86` declare:

```go
ExitCode int      // a FIELD, not a method
```

constructed at `worker/pool.go:691` as `&ExitError{ExitCode: exit.Code}`. A struct field named `ExitCode` does not satisfy `interface{ ExitCode() int }`, so `errors.As` never matches and **`notLoaded` returns `false` for every error, always**.

Both classifiers are fed by the same producer: `service/runner.go:46` → `worker/pool.go:691`. The census verified this by building a probe against the real package:

```
keepalive notLoaded matches:            false
controller launchctlExitCode matches:   true
```

`service/controller.go`'s classifier matches; `keepalive`'s does not. The two "disagreeing classifiers" named in root cause RC4 are worse than disagreeing — one of them is dead code that always returns the same answer.

## Consequences in production

- `AppKeepAlive.Uninstall` fails and **leaves the plist behind** when the agent is already unloaded (launchctl exit 3).
- `loaded` / `ensureUnloaded` / `Stop` fail whenever the agent is not currently loaded.

A third, weaker classifier sits at `keepalive.go:538`: `AppKeepAlive.Loaded` reads *any* error as "not loaded".

## Why the test suite cannot catch it

`service/keepalive_test.go:167`'s `shExit` helper fabricates an `*exec.ExitError` — which **does** have an `ExitCode() int` method. So the test exercises a type that production never produces. The test passes; the production path is dead. This is a test that cannot fail, and it hid a real defect for the life of the package.

Any fix must change the fixture to the type production actually produces, or the same blind spot survives the fix.

## Fix shape

This is the concrete, already-proven instance of the RC4 remediation: **one `launchctlOutcome` classifier**, in exactly one function, returning `Loaded | NotLoaded | Refused(reason) | InFlux | Unknown(code)`, with the field-paid code table in its godoc. Both existing classifiers route through it and the duplicates delete. Retry only `InFlux`.

ops.text: A single launchctlOutcome classifier exists in exactly one function; service/controller.go and service/keepalive.go both route through it and no second implementation remains

A test feeds the classifier the error type production actually produces (*worker.ExitError from worker/pool.go:691) — not a fabricated *exec.ExitError — and that test FAILS against the current HEAD implementation before the fix
AppKeepAlive.Uninstall removes the plist when the agent is already unloaded (launchctl exit 3), pinned by a test
Only InFlux is retried; every other outcome is terminal and its error names the observed state without prescribing anything it cannot prove
